title: Intelligent SLO-aligned fuse and safe delegation for dependency/model/tenant failures
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Transient spikes and dependency degradation (model/replica/region/3rd-party preprocessors) cause hard trips that either over-eject traffic or cause unsafe fallbacks. Goal: Implement an SLO-aligned, context-aware fuse that trips per dependency/model/tenant with hysteresis and safe delegation policies. The fuse should use workload-aware thresholds (latency/error quantiles + inferred customer SLOs), incorporate Bayesian smoothing to avoid flapping, and provide deterministic safe delegation: lower-fidelity model variant, cached responses, queued retry, or partial-response with structured error metadata. Must be observable, config-driven, and support simulation and dry-run evaluation before applying globally.
acceptance_criteria: Per-dependency per-model per-tenant fuse can be enabled via runtime config and defaults to dry-run
Trips calculated from 95/99 latency quantiles and p50/p90 error rates, with hysteresis windows configurable per tenant
When fuse trips, traffic is routed according to priority: 1) cached prefix response, 2) smaller/quantized model variant, 3) degraded structured response with error metadata; no silent failures
Dashboard shows false-positive rate, expected vs observed customer-visible SLO delta, and rollback counts
Simulation harness reproduces historical incidents with >80% fidelity and produces suggested trip thresholds
Automated canary untrip policy and human approval flow available in console for escalations
implementation_notes: Telemetry input: existing request-level metrics (latency_p50/p90/p95, token error counts, model qps) plus new per-tenant SLO annotations
Trip math: combine weighted z-score of latency and error rate with tenant SLO weight; use exponential moving average + Bayesian prior to smooth low-sample tenants
Hysteresis: two timers (soft-trip window, hard-trip lockout) with exponential backoff between re-eval attempts
Fallback actions: implement a fallback handler chain; handlers must declare deterministic cost and expected quality drop
Config: per-tenant policy objects stored in control plane and pushed to edge; support feature flags for dry-run/simulate/active
Runtime: keep decision logic lightweight; precompute per-route thresholds in routing plane to avoid per-request heavy math
Metrics & tags: include trip_reason, decision_path, fallback_taken, sample_count, region, model_version
decision_log: 2026-02-26: Chosen metric set: latency_p95 + error_rate + request_rate; rationale: covers latency spikes and error bursts that impact users
2026-03-01: Opted for Bayesian smoothing for low-volume tenants to avoid noisy trips; trade-off: slightly slower reaction to real regressions for tiny tenants
2026-03-04: Fallback priority settled: cache -> quantized model -> partial structured response -> queue retry. Reason: prefer costless/low-cost fallbacks first
2026-03-08: Decided to expose canary untrip via console with audit logs and a 2-person approval for P0 customer lanes
